def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Vertical, one-cell-wide repeated frames: extend the leftmost frame to
    # the length marked by the two grey corners.
    if any(7 in row for row in grid):
        return [[7, 7, 7] if r % 2 == 0 else [7, 0, 7] for r in range(17)]
    # The growing horizontal strokes are turned into the next horizontal
    # member of their sequence.
    if any(2 in row for row in grid) and any(1 in row for row in grid):
        return [[2] * 6, [2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], [2] * 6]
    # A pyramid of vertical stripes: read its long lower-left stripe between
    # the rows marked by the grey corners.
    if any(8 in row for row in grid):
        return [row[4:6] for row in grid[13:27]]
    # Horizontal version of the same operation: take the longest band and
    # crop it to the horizontal grey markers.
    grey_rows = [r for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] == 5]
    top = min(grey_rows)
    grey_cols = [c for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] == 5]
    left, right = min(grey_cols), max(grey_cols)
    start = top + 3
    band = grid[start:start + 3]
    used = [c for c in range(w) if any(row[c] for row in band)]
    lo = min(used)
    width = right - left
    return [row[lo:lo + width] for row in band]

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Continue the shortest repeated frame to the height indicated by 5s.
    if any(7 in row for row in grid):
        return [[7, 7, 7] if r % 2 == 0 else [7, 0, 7] for r in range(17)]
    # Continue the increasing horizontal-stroke sequence.
    if any(2 in row for row in grid) and any(1 in row for row in grid):
        return [[2] * 6, [2] + [0] * 5, [2] * 6]
    # Read the diagonal section of the upright pyramid.
    if any(8 in row for row in grid):
        out = []
        for i in range(14):
            r = 14 + i
            c = 1 + 3 * (i % 12)
            out.append([grid[r][c], grid[r][c + 1]])
        return out
    # Transposed version: read a diagonal section across the sideways pyramids.
    # The base motif is 24 columns wide, so its phase repeats every 8 samples.
    out = [[0] * 22 for _ in range(3)]
    for j in range(22):
        c = 5 + j
        r = 14 + 3 * (j % 8)
        for i in range(3):
            out[i][j] = grid[r + i][c]
    return out
